name: Singer lockstitch sewing machine
description: A sewing machine used a straight eye-pointed needle and reciprocating shuttle to make a lockstitch; commercial machines were built for manufacturing trades.

impact.note: Made existing lockstitch sewing practical and sold it across continents; garment making was reorganised around it and ready-made clothing trades grew.

date.label: 12 August 1851
date.basis: The source reports the date for this scoped event or archaeological context.

events.statement: Singer’s sewing-machine model received a United States patent on 12 August 1851.

evidence.supports: Singer’s sewing-machine model received a United States patent on 12 August 1851.
The source attributes this contribution to isaac-singer.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated case currently researched, not a claim of the capability’s original invention or global priority.

caveats: Patent date identifies a documented model and claims, not the invention of all lockstitch sewing or the start date of all commercial sales.

research.note: Independent review checked the Smithsonian’s collection account as exposed through its indexed full-text record and a separate Smithsonian archive catalogue for the patent date. The museum does not date the shop’s commercial output to the precise patent day.
